scope: headless priority preemption and per-worker Windows QoS; no UI automation
changes: PDFium/metadata retain immediate kill behavior, but now use the same per-wire notice to prevent late Ready from releasing the slot before kill completes
PPE internal priority preemption uses cooperative cancel and retries after foreground
100ms acknowledgement grace after control send, owned-worker kill fallback
notice scoped by pid and wire request id prevents late kill racing the next request
ordinary user cancellation is not auto-retried
retain document affinity while worker survives
HighQoS only in render-worker process; no affinity/priority-class/registry/power-plan changes

defaults.cpu_diagnostic_env: PRYNX_WORKER_CPU_PROBE=1 (debug only, requires PRYNX_PERF=1 and writable log)

baseline_red.reason: PPE process changed during internal preemption

findings: Slow samples end replay/encode on logical CPUs 12..15 (EfficiencyClass 0); fast samples use 0..11 (EfficiencyClass 1).
Same binary policy A/B in order system/high then high/system: foreground after priority preemption 4814..4936ms under system versus 2236..2338ms under high, identical PNG.
Under identical HighQoS worker: old manager foreground 2248..2314ms with worker restart; new manager 2236..2338ms retaining PID. Small sample, no general speedup claimed for preemption alone.
corrections: The initial ~2x slowdown was not proven to originate in the cooperative-cancel code: old manager and no-preemption controls also showed it.
Running outside sandbox alone is not a sufficient explanation/fix; an outside priority probe remained slow under automatic/system QoS.
Executable copy path did not explain the slowdown. QoS A/B and CPU topology provide the concrete evidence; no Windows global settings were changed.
limitations: In zero-background-lane diagnostic runs, background_thumbnail_cold is the first background request but its session is already warm; do not interpret the inherited phase label as a cold session
Timing is native parent/worker, not UI presentation time.
PRYNX_RENDER_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0 is a one-lane simulation on this 32GiB machine, not a physical low-RAM test.
Priority 20 is an intentionally non-preemptible control; production prefetch policy uses background priority >=100.
Only two measured foreground samples per QoS in the counterbalanced comparison, not P95 or a whole-corpus throughput gate.
100ms starts after sending cancellation; failed OS termination is reported, not guaranteed to stop a broken OS.
Separate interactive/background sessions and actual sidebar integration are not yet unified.
All noisy/control samples retained. Existing app binary remains unchanged.
